correctness.rationale: A left translation of the support left-multiplies the operator by an invertible permutation. Thus it suffices to take supports {1,a,b}, each unordered original support contributing three distinguished normalizations to the translation count, giving weight 48/3=16 per normalized pair. I independently rebuilt the multiplication table using one rational-versus-quadratic scale per quaternion, formed the three translated columns for each of the 1,081 normalized supports, and computed all their ranks by exact integer row elimination, without orbit rank transfer or modular inference. Every signature row, the nullity histogram and the mixed-coset histogram agree. The 10,240 singular supports equal the total less the 7,056 invertible ones. As the table shows only signature (3,3,3) at nullity 32, counting the 64 distinct cosets of the four order-three subgroups, each visibly of that signature, establishes the maximum and its exact locus. The mixed index-two test is invariant under normalizing the support and equivalent to at least one of a,b lying outside H.
residual_risks: This is the complete finite unweighted three-support census, not a classification for weights, more taps, or other group sizes.
The frozen modular ranks are corroborative only; the independent replay uses exact rank-preserving integer operations for all normalized supports.

value.rationale: Three-tap invertibility and defect for the natural regular convolution algebra on a binary polyhedral group are precise support invariants. The order-only rule avoids a matrix computation per triple and is not automatic from group membership or character degrees. The cross-coset examples with nullity five in particular are structurally impossible via the known doubled tetrahedral nullities; their counts and the split into mixed signatures address a genuine gap. The inherited maximum is not the justification for value.
residual_risks: This does not prove order-only determination for other groups or for weighted triples.
